title: Retry Attempts Aggregated into One Latency Sample
pattern: A retry loop runs inside the same timing block used to record per-request latency, so multiple attempts are recorded as one sample and the failures are not counted anywhere.
why_bad: A request that failed twice and succeeded on the third attempt looks like one slow request. Failure rate disappears into the latency distribution, and per-attempt latency (what the downstream actually delivers) cannot be recovered.
detection: A retry loop (`while res.is_err()`, `for attempt in 0..n`, retry combinators) nested between an `Instant::now()` and the `elapsed()` that feeds a per-request latency metric, with no per-attempt latency or retry counter recorded.
counterexample: User-facing transaction latency where total time including retries is the declared SLO metric, recorded alongside a retry/attempt counter.
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!* (2007), Ch. 4, §4.10, p. 48; Brendan Gregg, *Systems Performance* (2013), Ch. 2, §2.5, p. 34.
